subject: Mislabelling of individuals and populations in output of gl2snapp

messages.author: cb1c123aa86bc7d5
messages.subject: Mislabelling of individuals and populations in output of gl2snapp
parts:
Hi Arthur and Bernd,

I've found an error in the gl2snapp conversion tool that has really messed up my SNAPP runs. I'm not sure if it's something specific to what I did but it is something to check in the code for this function.

The order of individuals in the original genlight object is not sorted by alphabetical order or by population. But when I convert to SNAPP using gl2snapp, the NEXUS file has individuals grouped by population and ordered alphabetically. I had just taken this for granted as a useful bonus but after several of my SNAPP runs produced spurious results, I went back to check where I could have made a mistake. I looked at the genotypes of the individuals in the NEXUS file and they did not match the individual genotypes in the genlight object. I checked the source code for the gl2snapp function and there is no specification for individuals and populations to be ordered in the output so I don't know where the disconnect occurs but it means the individuals and populations in my NEXUS file are completely mislabelled. 

I've attached a screenshot of my genlight object as a matrix and the resulting NEXUS file. 

Please let me know if I can provide any more details. Hope this can get sorted!

Cheers,

Yael

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Mislabelling of individuals and populations in output of gl2snapp
parts:
Hi Yael,

Yes, this is true. Arthur - at some point I sent you a re-write of this function that just stripped out the reordering by population? Then it worked fine, just exported individuals in the pre-existing order in the gl.

Cheers,

Renee

messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Mislabelling of individuals and populations in output of gl2snapp
parts: This was it, if anyone wants it. Worked fine for my SNAPP runs. It's actually a super easy fix, I just removed line 65 in the function where the dataframe was sorted by population. There is no reason this actually needs to be sorted by population for snapp, so it works fine without it. The population assignments within beauti are exactly the same amount of work whether it's sorted by population or not.
